title: Israeli Forces Launch Large-Scale Raid on Qalandiya Refugee Camp Near Jerusalem
excerpt: The IDF detained several Palestinians after storming the camp in occupied East Jerusalem, using tear gas, stun grenades, and live ammunition in an operation that drew condemnation from Palestinian officials.
body:
• Israeli forces launched a large-scale raid on the Qalandiya refugee camp near occupied East Jerusalem on Tuesday, detaining several Palestinians and deploying tear gas, stun grenades, and live ammunition.
  • The operation reportedly began when border police entered the camp to map a UNRWA building, and escalated after a Palestinian gunman opened fire on the unit.
  • At least two Palestinians were seriously wounded, including a civilian hit by Israeli fire and a resident who sustained a head injury during a raid on a vocational training institute.
  • The camp, home to roughly 14,000 displaced Palestinians, has been a flashpoint amid intensified Israeli security operations across the West Bank.

Israeli forces launched what officials described as a large-scale operation in the Qalandiya refugee camp near occupied East Jerusalem on Tuesday, detaining several Palestinians in a raid that involved live ammunition, tear gas, and stun grenades across densely populated residential areas.

The Qalandiya camp, located between Jerusalem and Ramallah and home to approximately 14,000 displaced Palestinians, has been the site of repeated Israeli military incursions in recent months as security operations across the occupied West Bank have intensified.

How the Raid Unfolded

According to Middle East Eye, Israeli border police initially entered the camp to map a United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA) building in the nearby Kafr Aqab neighbourhood. During the operation, a Palestinian man opened fire on the police unit, prompting an immediate military escalation.

The Israeli military dispatched additional troops to secure the area. The gunman was shot; his condition has not been confirmed. Israeli units also stormed a vocational training institute opposite the camp, according to a statement from the Jerusalem governorate.

The Wafa news agency reported that a young Palestinian civilian was seriously wounded by Israeli fire. Another resident sustained a severe head injury during the raid on the training institute.

A Pattern of Escalation

The Qalandiya operation is part of a broader pattern of Israeli military activity across the occupied West Bank that has accelerated since October 2023. According to official Palestinian figures, Israeli military operations and settler violence in the West Bank have killed more than 1,175 Palestinians, injured over 12,900, and resulted in roughly 24,000 arrests since that date.

In a previous large-scale operation in January, Israeli forces raided homes and shops in the Shu'fat refugee camp, detaining at least 25 Palestinians. A separate operation targeting Kafr Aqab and the boundaries of Qalandiya resulted in the demolition of 70 Palestinian structures, which the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights said appeared to be preparation for settlement projects.

"The unlawful deportation or transfer of a population living under occupation is a war crime, and, under specific circumstances, may constitute a crime against humanity."

— UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights

Israeli and Palestinian Responses

The IDF confirmed what it called a "limited" operation in Qalandiya aimed at "thwarting terror," according to the Times of Israel. The military said the raid was part of routine security activity to arrest suspects and counter militant infrastructure.

Palestinian officials condemned the operation as an excessive use of force. The Jerusalem governorate called on the international community to intervene to halt what it described as an escalation of attacks against Palestinian civilians. Human rights organizations have repeatedly documented the use of live fire and crowd-control weapons in densely populated refugee camps.

India's Diplomatic Balancing Act

The continued escalation in the West Bank complicates India's diplomatic positioning. New Delhi maintains strategic partnerships with both Israel and several Arab states, and the Indian diaspora across the Gulf — numbering over 8 million — has a direct stake in regional stability. India has consistently called for a two-state solution while maintaining defence and technology ties with Israel.

What to Watch

The raid comes days after Hamas announced it had agreed to terms that could end hostilities in Gaza, including provisions for disarmament and Israeli withdrawal. Whether that framework extends to the West Bank, where Israeli settlement expansion and military operations continue largely independently of Gaza negotiations, remains an open question. Observers are watching for signs of coordinated protests or retaliatory attacks that could signal a broader escalation beyond isolated confrontations.
nri_angle: The escalation raises concerns among Indians with business and diplomatic ties to the region, and adds urgency to India's balancing act between its relationships with Israel and the Arab world.
